struct.title: Cryo-EM structure of the SST-14-bound SSTR2-miniGq-scFv16 complex

pubmed.rcsb_pubmed_abstract_text: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) modulate every aspect of physiological functions mainly through activating heterotrimeric G proteins. A majority of GPCRs promiscuously couple to multiple G protein subtypes. Here we validate that in addition to the well-known G <sub>i/o </sub> pathway, somatostatin receptor 2 and 5 (SSTR2 and SSTR5) couple to the G <sub>q/11 </sub> pathway and show that smaller ligands preferentially activate the G <sub>i/o </sub> pathway. We further determined cryo-electron microscopy structures of the SSTR2‒G <sub>o </sub> and SSTR2‒G <sub>q </sub> complexes bound to octreotide and SST-14. Structural and functional analysis revealed that G protein selectivity of SSTRs is not only determined by structural elements in the receptor-G protein interface, but also by the conformation of the agonist-binding pocket. Accordingly, smaller ligands fail to stabilize a broader agonist-binding pocket of SSTRs that is required for efficient G <sub>q/11 </sub> coupling but not G <sub>i/o </sub> coupling. Our studies facilitate the design of drugs with selective G protein signaling to improve therapeutic efficacy.
